reason: The passage is predominantly told from David's perspective as a leader. The text explicitly describes his men's ingratitude when they threaten to stone him after the Amalekite raid on Ziklag (וַתֵּ֨צֶר לְדָוִ֜ד מְאֹ֗ד כִּֽי־ אָמְר֤וּ הָעָם֙ לְסָקְל֔וֹ - 'It was very distressing to David, for the people spoke of stoning him'). Despite this disloyalty and ingratitude from his men—who blame him for the disaster affecting their families—David strengthens himself in the Lord and leads them to pursue the raiders. This exemplifies a leader managing an ungrateful populace.
